claims: The frozen Small Shop sources compile through the private LinkML adapter, neutral contract representation, canonical facts, immutable ContractView, and an identified partial EffectiveContract.

Canonical machine and policy artifacts own the measured event, check, transition, effect, refusal, and verdict behavior; the generic Python interpreter executes those artifacts without fixture vocabulary, arbitrary callbacks, ledger authority, or graph mutation access.

One closed immutable KnowledgeChangeSet binds the exact contract, base history and state, retained source and evidence closure, zero-based operations, valid time, local dependencies, supersession references, and its content identity.

One JSONL semantic/protocol history is the retained authority. Replay begins from an empty graph and reconstructs the accepted Small Shop state and canonical receipt without ambient fixture or program files.
The accepted view contains SalesOrder O1, InventoryUnit X1, and OrderContainsUnit contains:O1:X1; all 140 focused tests pass and final independent audit reports no P0 through P2 defect.
limitations: This is private research-local evidence, not a public compiler API, stable wire format, package, release, production Assent cutover, or cross-language conformance result.

The current proof covers initial entity and relation creation plus structural current-state replay. It does not implement general mapping, correction, update, delete, public bitemporal queries, GraphRecipe, OTTR, Prolog, effects, observation, or Semantic Re-entry.
The full repository pytest suite and package checks were not completed for this milestone under the operator-selected Pareto gate.

why: The completion receipt and mechanical gates prove one real source-to-contract-to-change-set-to-history-to-query path while retaining the public, packaging, correction, effect, and Semantic Re-entry boundaries as explicit future work.
